notes: Production in Europe ended in 2018; in China the first generation was built until 2020 and sold as the Tiguan Silk Road alongside the second generation (Wikipedia).
In North America the first generation covered model years 2009–2016, and was sold on for 2017–2018 as the Tiguan Limited alongside the second generation.
Wikipedia dates the facelift to 2011 (Geneva) but heads the section 'Facelift (2012)' because it applied to 2012 models; Volkswagen dates the unveiling to 2011.

Sales start: Volkswagen says the market launch followed the 2007 IAA premiere in the same year; English Wikipedia says the Tiguan went on sale in Europe in early 2008, and German Wikipedia gives sales from August 2007. The manufacturer statement is recorded.

The facelift was presented at the 2011 Geneva show; German Wikipedia dates the revised model to July 2011. Wikipedia (de) gives a body length range of 4,426–4,457 mm; no single length is recorded. The Chinese long-wheelbase version (2010–2017 per de.wikipedia) has a 2,684 mm wheelbase.

changes.text: The Tiguan moved to Volkswagen's Modular Transverse Toolkit (MQB).
changes.quote: The SUV was now constructed using the Modular Transverse Toolkit (MQB) for the first time.

changes.text: The short-wheelbase model is 50 kg lighter than the first generation.
changes.quote: which is 50 kg (110 lb) lighter than the outgoing Tiguan

changes.text: It is 60 mm longer and 30 mm wider, with a wheelbase 77 mm longer.
changes.quote: while also 60 mm (2.4 in) longer, 30 mm (1.2 in) wider, and its wheelbase is extended by 77 mm (3.0 in)

changes.text: A long-wheelbase version with up to seven seats was added in 2017, with a wheelbase extended by 110 mm.
changes.quote: The product line was revamped again in 2017 with the debut of a second Tiguan Model– an XL version with a wheelbase extended by 110 mm, up to seven seats, and a bespoke design.

revealed.quote: The updated Tiguan was released on 30 June 2020, along with the introduction of the Tiguan R and Tiguan eHybrid.

changes.text: A plug-in hybrid, the Tiguan eHybrid, was added.
changes.quote: New Tiguan now also available with plug-in hybrid

changes.text: A separate Tiguan R model was offered for the first time.
changes.quote: The SUV will now also be available as a separate Tiguan R model for the very first time.

changes.text: The third-generation modular infotainment matrix (MIB3) was introduced.
changes.quote: New infotainment systems: third-generation modular infotainment matrix (MIB3) offers the best possible online connectivity for the Tiguan

changes.text: The front end was redesigned with a wider grille and LED headlights, and the badge placed centrally.
changes.quote: The bonnet is more concise in its appearance and the new radiator grille with LED headlights is wider, with the new Volkswagen badge positioned centrally at the front.

changes.text: At the rear, the Tiguan lettering moved to a central position below the badge.
changes.quote: At the rear, the Tiguan lettering is now in a prominent central position below the VW badge.

revealed.quote: Eine überarbeitete Version des Allspace wurde im Mai 2021 präsentiert.

changes.text: A redesigned front lengthened the Tiguan Allspace to 4,723 mm, 22 mm more; interior dimensions are unchanged.
changes.quote: Visually, it features a modified front, which has been extended to 4,723 mm (an extra 22 mm) for design purposes. The generous interior dimensions remain unchanged.

changes.text: IQ.LIGHT LED matrix headlights became available on the Tiguan Allspace for the first time.
changes.quote: For the first time, the Tiguan Allspace can now be ordered with IQ.LIGHT LED matrix headlights.

changes.text: IQ.DRIVE Travel Assist was offered in the Tiguan Allspace for the first time.
changes.quote: Partly automated driving is made possible by IQ.DRIVE Travel Assist that is used for the first time in the Tiguan Allspace.

notes: Market distinction: in Europe the long-wheelbase version (codes BW2/BJ2 per Wikipedia) is sold as the Tiguan Allspace beside the normal-wheelbase Tiguan; in North America only the long-wheelbase body was offered and it was called simply 'Tiguan'; in China it was the Tiguan L (built by SAIC-VW), with the Tiguan X coupé SUV derived from it.
Wikipedia also lists a model code 'AX1' next to AD1 without explaining it; it is not recorded here.
Volkswagen states the long-wheelbase version has a wheelbase 110 mm longer; Wikipedia gives 109 mm (2,681 vs 2,791 mm).
Sales start: Volkswagen gives April 2016 for the sales launch; German Wikipedia gives January 2016 for the start of sales of the second generation. The manufacturer date is recorded.
Production: Wikipedia gives 2016–2024 for the generation overall; the Chinese Tiguan L continued after that and the Tiguan X was built 2020–2026.
The North American model was updated for the 2022 model year (Wikipedia).
The 2020 facelift of the normal-wheelbase model and the 2021 update of the Tiguan Allspace are recorded as separate revisions; German Wikipedia notes the Allspace kept the old design until 2021.

Long wheelbase: German Wikipedia says the Tiguan Allspace was first shown at the Detroit show in January 2017 and the European version at Geneva in March 2017, with sales in North America from summer 2017 and in Europe from September 2017; the Chinese Tiguan L was on sale from 18 January 2017.

Commons: no separate category for the 2021 Tiguan Allspace update was checked; the Allspace category covers both versions. Commons also has 'Category:Volkswagen Tiguan L' and 'Category:Volkswagen Tiguan II (North America)' for the long-wheelbase versions in China and North America.

notes: Volkswagen said in September 2023 that the third generation would roll off the line in Wolfsburg from fall 2023 and reach the market in the first quarter of 2024; Wikipedia gives production from 2024. European pre-sales opened in November 2023 (Volkswagen).

North America: the 2025 'Tiguan' sold in the US and Canada is a long-wheelbase car that Wikipedia describes as nearly identical to the Chinese-market Tayron L rather than the European Tiguan, with two rows of seats only. It is kept in this generation with its own dimensions record; no separate model code or North American press release could be read (media.vw.com renders only with JavaScript). North American model years are not recorded because no readable source states them explicitly.
China: the third generation is sold as the long-wheelbase Tiguan L Pro, alongside the previous Tiguan L.
European powertrain figures are from Volkswagen's German-market releases; market recorded as EU.

Dimensions conflict: English Wikipedia gives 4,551 mm length, 1,842 mm width, 1,640 mm height and 2,681 mm wheelbase for the European model; German Wikipedia gives 4,539 mm length, 1,842–1,859 mm width, 1,656–1,658 mm height and 2,677–2,680 mm wheelbase. Volkswagen's readable releases give no absolute figures (only 'around three centimetres' longer than before). The German figure is recorded; it should be checked against the Volkswagen press kit (PDF, not readable by our tool).
